## Analysis

Hand-written test fixture of a CP-1A Handoff for the synthetic Primary pack `czr-2026q2-primary`. Caesars is being sold: Fertitta Entertainment agreed on May 27, 2026 to buy every share for $31.00 in cash in a transaction valued at about 17.6 billion including about 11.9 billion of Caesars' debt [C1] [C2], financed with Fertitta's equity, the assumed debt and new committed debt [C3]; the new Senior Secured Term Loan B of 3,000 is in marketing at initial talk [C4]. After closing Caesars delists and becomes private [C5], so a public-company disclosure regime ends and the owner's financial policy becomes the main governance question.

The earnings and the fixed charges sit in different places. Regional is the largest segment by revenue in the first half [C6], Las Vegas the one whose Adjusted EBITDA fell most in the second quarter [C7], and every resort runs on leased real estate: the VICI and GLPI leases require 1.4 billion of rent in 2026, escalating with CPI [C8]. The strongest fact against a debt-funded buyout is that rent, not debt service, is the first fixed charge; what would settle it is the owner's post-closing capital structure and any sale-leaseback or asset disposal plan, which the pack does not contain.
